text_blocks.snippet: A cat's age in human years is not a strict "one cat year equals seven human years" ratio. Cats age much faster during their first two years. By their first birthday, they are roughly 15 years old, and by their second birthday, they are about 24 years old. PetMD
snippet_highlighted_words: one cat year equals seven human years

text_blocks.snippet: After year two, cats age at a more consistent rate, adding about 4 human years for every calendar year. PetMD
Cat Age to Human Age Chart
A breakdown of popular ages and their approximate human equivalents: PetMD +2

list.snippet: First Year: Fast physical growth and learning; a 1-year-old cat is comparable to a human teenager.
Second Year: Emotional and physical maturity; a 2-year-old is essentially in their mid-20s.
Subsequent Years: Each year after 24 adds exactly 4 human years to their age. PetMD +1

perspectives.title: Cats age much differently than humans. A cat reaches the equivalent of about 15 human years by its first birthday and around 24 human years by age 2. After that, each additional cat year is roughly equal to 4 human years. That means a 10 year old cat is comparable to a 56 year old human, while an 18 year old cat is roughly equivalent to an 88 year old person. Understanding your cat’s age can help you better appreciate the different stages of their life, from playful kitten to senior companion.
